source_text: Si Christus mutavit officia genitalium, Adam ea pervertisse credatur; si Christus aliquid correxit in sensibus carnis, aestimetur eos Adae culpa turbasse; si Christus fecit medicinam ire per propaginem, dicatur Adam per generationem transmisisse delictum.
pass_a_gloss: If Christ changed the functions of the genitals, let Adam be believed to have perverted them; if Christ corrected anything in the senses of the flesh, let it be estimated that Adam's fault disturbed them; if Christ made medicine go through the stock, let Adam be said to have transmitted an offense through generation.

lemmas.lexica: LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: If Christ changed the functions of the genitals, let it be believed that Adam corrupted them. If Christ corrected something in bodily sensations, let it be supposed that Adam’s fault disturbed them. If Christ made medicine pass through descent, let it be said that Adam transmitted the offense through generation.

choices.why: Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
